newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN RUPEE STEADY V DLR IN SPOT, FORWARDS SLIP.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN RUPEE STEADY V DLR IN SPOT, FORWARDS SLIP.

text.p: The rupee was steady against the dollar in quiet late morning trade on Friday, dealers said.
Spot deals during the day were mostly at 35.7150.
Some dealers said Oil and Natural Gas Corporation was bidding for dollars, but company officials were not immediately available for comment.
Forward premiums fell by five to six paise but were steady in latest trades, dealers said.
Forwards had crashed on Thursday in the absence of Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention.
RBI's surprise intervention in the forward dollar market earlier this week had pushed up premiums.

"With no change in interest rate outlook the spurt in forward premiums came as a windfall to corporates without in any way changing the market sentiment on a strong rupee," Societe Generale bank said in an India commentary.

"Recently, in nine out of 10 times, RBI stepped in to halt the rupee's gains. One out of 10 days when RBI stays out is the crucial day for the rupee to stage a fresh rally past the psychological levels," it said.
It said RBI's spot intervention at lower and lower levels showed that time was ripe for testing the 35.70 mark and target the 35.67 level.
